acceptedWorkstreams.title: Give each writer an exclusive angle: five outlets, five different proofs of Zedu
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The accepted approach pitches one story; editors often decline what several outlets get at once. Approach: write five pitches where each writer gets a different verified Zedu proof - one on pricing in naira, one on the product build, one on what replaces WhatsApp classes, one on a measured fact, one on the team story - each marked exclusive while held, with what happens if they pass. Every fact in every pitch links to a source checked that day. Tasks: five proof-first pitch drafts (press), outlet-exclusivity tracker (research).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Pitch named writers with one sourced Zedu story, then follow up once
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
Coverage comes from pitching specific writers, not mass-mailing newsrooms. Steps, each a finishable task:
1. Press-ready basics (content): a 100-word boilerplate, a one-page fact sheet using only team-confirmed numbers, and 5 current screenshots. Reuse the fact sheet and press kit work already open in this project rather than redoing it.
2. Target list (research): 20 writers or editors at news sites, blogs and newsletters who covered African edtech, remote learning or bootcamps in the last 90 days, each with a link to that article and a public contact route.
3. Pitches (press): one short pitch per writer (under 150 words) that ties Zedu to the angle they already cover, plus one plain press release for outlets that take them.
4. Send and follow up (press): send in two batches, follow up once after 5 working days, and log each reply and any published mention with its URL.
Success is counted the way the goal says: published articles or mentions with links. Nothing goes in a pitch that the team has not confirmed.

pendingIdeas.title: Pitch only reporters who covered African edtech in the last six months, with their recent article linked in the list
pendingIdeas.description: Pitch success depends on reaching the person already on the beat, not the outlet's general inbox. Approach: list writers at outlets such as TechCabal, Techpoint Africa, Benjamindada.com, Disrupt Africa and Rest of World who published on African edtech, bootcamps or learning tools in the last six months. Record their recent article link and date, their beat, and the public pitch channel (no private contacts). Rank them by how closely their recent work matches Zedu's story. Done: the ranked list of 15-20 writers with evidence, and the angle each one should get.
